rationale: The first fixed-node comparison gave different feasible costs in only two pairs. Test whether the difference survives a stronger two-dispatch prefetch with an economically sensible single-versus-grouped service option and a real time limit. Keep the earlier baseline unchanged.
design: All versions start with the same feasible rollout. The measured online clock begins before building a fresh planner, excluding only Python imports and the scenario's public input. A process alarm returns the last available fully evaluated incumbent. A predeclared always-executable serial default is available at time zero; its expected cost can be assessed after the deadline and does not inform planning. Use the same legal actions, costs, order, fallback hierarchy, cost lower bound and two-dispatch portfolio for generic and continuation-equivalent search. The compute-only experiment runs after timed natural tasks on this host settle. Interleave solver order across repetitions. Report overruns and elapsed percentiles, candidate quality and proven optimality separately; a fractional state expansion is never a result.
limits: One host, Python implementation, synthetic public stochastic work orders replaying genuine cost anchors. Both exact when complete. A comparison with equal canonicalization is the same algorithm. No robot, physical duration claim, fresh inference, hidden semantic answer or independent benchmark.
